standard_prerequisites: the completeness theorem for first-order logic without identity and the term model it constructs
the Henkin construction delivering a structure whose domain is the closed terms of the extended language
denumerability of the term set of a countable language
core_obligations: Prove that a consistent set of sentences of first-order logic without identity has a model whose domain is infinite and enumerable
proof_roadmap: Run the completeness construction: for consistent Gamma without identity sentences, the structure M it delivers has domain exactly the term set of the extended language L'
The term set of the countable language L' is enumerable, so the domain of M is enumerable; the construction also makes it infinite, so M is a denumerable model of Gamma
difficulty_reason: The argument reuses the completeness construction; the work is in recalling that the delivered term model has the term set as domain and that identity absence keeps the domain the full term set.
